## Shared context (already established by Superior; do not redo, do verify anything you rely on)

**How the web page loads.** `web/index.html` lines 762-841 are the script tags, all classic `<script src>` except the three `type="module"` tags for `src/scenestats.js` (which needs its own top-level scope because it declares `const path` like `src/packs.js`). Order: `lib/nodeshim.js`, `../src/packs.js`, `lib/adopt.js`, `../src/takes.js`, the three module tags, then `../src/align.js`, `score.js`, `camtrack.js`, `reellayout.js`, `credits.js`, `collab.js`, `showcase.js`, `flags.js`, `handles.js`, `ads.js`, `offers.js`, `rendergate.js`, then `lib/unzip.js`, `takeseed.js`, `takefile.js`, `takewrite.js`, `store.js`, `packsource.js`, `codecs.js`, `audio.js`, `schedule.js`, `transport.js`, `recorder.js`, `webconfig.js`, `native.js`, `api.js`, `report.js`, `scenedigest.js`, `zipwrite.js`, then the view scripts **`app.js`, `booth.js`, `editor.js`, `account.js`, `ads.js`, `billing.js`, `collabweb.js`, `start.js`**. `start.js` (10 lines) calls `window.bootApp()`, which `app.js:1909` sets (`window.bootApp = boot;`) — the only `window.*` assignment in app.js, booth.js or collabweb.js. CSP: `script-src 'self'`, `style-src 'self'` (no inline scripts, no injected styles).

**The lib/ convention.** Every `web/lib/*.js` is `'use strict';` then `window.Name = (function () { … })();` — one namespace object per file, private scope, a file-head comment saying what it is and what it deliberately does not restate (e.g. `lib/audio.js` → `window.Engine`, `lib/transport.js` → `window.Transport`, `lib/api.js` → `window.Api`, `lib/report.js` → `window.Report`). The three view scripts are the opposite shape: bare top-level `const`/`let`/`function` declarations (app.js 92, booth.js 66, collabweb.js 108) sharing the page's global lexical scope, called bare from each other (booth.js calls app.js's `state`, `$`, `toast`, `showView`, `setHeader`…; app.js calls booth.js's `wireBooth`, `enterBooth`…; collabweb.js is called by app/booth/account/editor). Classic scripts share top-level `let`/`const`/`function` across tags; ES modules do not — a split must keep those bare names reachable, so **do not propose modules unless you prove every cross-file reference survives** (the safe default is more classic scripts in the same tag order). A top-level `const` moved to a later tag is a temporal-dead-zone hazard for any earlier tag that reads it at load time (not inside a function called later) — name each such case in Risks.
